title: Evaluation of the effectiveness of a digital support tool (Mika-App) for cancer patients under clinical routine conditions at the Comprehensive Cancer Center Central Germany (CCCG): Effects on self-management skills, psychological distress, and quality of life
summary: The study examines how effective the Mika app is for cancer patients as part of routine clinical care in Leipzig and Jena. The focus is on self-management, psychological stress and quality of life. It also examines which factors (e.g. age, gender, digital health literacy) influence usage. To this end, 300 patients are randomly assigned to a group with app use or a waiting list. The effect is compared over three points in time (start, after 3 and 6 months). The aim is to better adapt the app to the needs of those affected.

interventions.name: Randomized intervention group (MIKA app use from t0 baseline), data collected at three measurement points t0, t1 (after 3 months) and t2 (after 6 months)
Randomized waiting list control group (MIKA app use after 3 months), data collected at three measurement points t0, t1 (after 3 months) and t2 (after 6 months)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis of a solid tumor (C00- C80, C97) or hematological cancer (C81-C96) according to ICD-10, confirmed via the hospital documentation system
- Age of at least 18 years at the time of study inclusion
Exclusion criteria:
- physically, mentally or cognitively incapable of consenting to participate in the study
